note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Young adult with 2–3 days of exertional shortness of breath, wheeze and cough starting while running; using salbutamol (blue) with inadequate relief.
- Plan: GP face-to-face review in next few days; interim increase preventer inhaler dose and use salbutamol PRN; go to A&E if breathing worsens.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute asthma exacerbation, onset 2–3 days ago during running; worse with brisk walking.
- Symptoms: shortness of breath, wheeze, cough. No sputum production.
- Current inhaler use: salbutamol (blue) as needed (patient reports both PRN and daily use); preventer (brown, Clenil) used twice daily.
- Baseline peak flow reported ~380 L/min when well; patient has not performed peak flow since symptoms began.
- No prior hospital admissions for asthma; last significant attack ~3–4 years ago; no recollection of prior oral steroids or antibiotics.
- Assessment: mild–moderate exacerbation suspected; inadequate response to salbutamol at home.
- Immediate management advised: increase preventer (Clenil) to 4 puffs twice daily while awaiting review; use salbutamol every 2–4 hours PRN; seek A&E if breathing acutely worsens before review.
- Planned face-to-face GP review for chest examination, measured peak flow, and consideration of oral steroids and/or antibiotics based on findings.

Issue 2:
- Suboptimal recent asthma review and monitoring.
- Last asthma review with practice nurse ~2 years ago.
- Patient performs peak flow only occasionally; no recent objective measurement during this exacerbation.
- Plan: formal asthma review at face-to-face appointment including peak flow, inhaler technique check, medication reconciliation and adjustment as needed.

Issue 3:
- Atopic history: patient reports hay fever; possible personal eczema (family history: brother asthmatic, sister with eczema). Patient uses topical preparations.
- Medications mentioned for skin: Cetraben and hydrocortisone (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- No medication allergies reported.

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient using PRN; doctor advised up to every 2–4 hours PRN).
- Clenil (brown preventer inhaler) — current use twice daily; dose not documented. Clinician advised increase to 4 puffs twice daily while awaiting review.
- Cetraben (topical) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hydrocortisone (topical) — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No medication allergies reported.
- Patient reports hay fever (environmental allergy).

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (stable until recent 2–3 day exacerbation).
- No history of hospital admissions for asthma reported.
- No known prior oral steroid use reported.

Social History:
- Patient runs (reported exertional symptoms while running).
- No formal smoking, alcohol, living arrangement details documented.

Preventative History:
- Asthma review approximately 2 years ago.
- No other preventative care (cervical screening, mammogram, PSA, FOBT, bone density, vaccinations, optometry, or skin checks) documented in the consult.

Physical Examination:
- No examination performed during this consult.
- No vitals, oxygen saturation, or objective respiratory measurements recorded during the visit.

Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face GP appointment within the next few days for chest exam, peak flow measurement, inhaler technique check, and medication review.
- Interim measures:
  - Increase preventer (Clenil) to 4 puffs twice daily (as advised by clinician).
  - Continue/use salbutamol (blue inhaler) as needed, up to every 2–4 hours; recognize that frequent use indicates poor control.
  - Advise patient to present to A&E immediately if breathing worsens before GP review.
- At face-to-face visit clinician may prescribe oral steroids and/or antibiotics depending on assessment and peak flow.
- Encourage regular peak flow monitoring and record readings for the appointment.

document_quality — Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: current vitals (respiratory rate, heart rate, oxygen saturation), objective current peak flow during symptoms, exact inhaler drug doses and formulations, inhaler technique assessment, smoking and alcohol history, confirmation of eczema diagnosis, medication dosages and routes.
- Internal conflicts noted:
  - Patient described salbutamol use both "as and when" (PRN) and "using it every day" (conflict regarding frequency).
  - Initial medication list included an unclear item ("Flanel Bactroban") that patient later corrected to Cetraben and hydrocortisone.
- Transcript quality: several short inaudible/unclear segments and occasional overlap; overall sufficient to document history and plan but lacks objective measurements and some medication details.
